subject: Summit Health — topology & SLOs: post-call summary + action items
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@summithealth.ai>, Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@summithealth.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Summit Health — topology & SLOs: post-call summary + action items

Hi Maya / Rahul,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the clear articulation of the problems you’re seeing. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to capture next steps.

Key pain points (what you told us)
- Intermittent high tail latency during morning spikes (30–45 minutes) causing UI timeouts at the clinician portal.
- Need predictable throughput for batch ingestion (telemetry + notes) during nightly processing windows.
- Compliance constraints: PHI-in-transit, desire for US-only data residency and SOC 2 evidence.

High-level goals
- 99th percentile generation latency <= 350 ms for short clinical prompts (~128 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target: 300 requests/min with bursts to 600 reqs/min for peak windows (avg payload ~512 tokens).
- Canary rollouts with automatic fallbacks to smaller model family under tail pressure.

Model & topology notes from call
- Primary model class: ~70B dense / quantized (we discussed Llama2-70B Q4_0-like profiles) for extraction/reranking tasks; fallback to 13B quantized for cost/latency fallback.
- Proposal: Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 with 2 worker pools:
  1) Low-latency pool (pinned GPU type) for interactive clinician traffic, aggressive KV cache & small batching.
  2) Throughput pool for bulk/nightly jobs with larger batching and pre-warming.
- Smart routing policy: latency-first for interactive endpoints, cost-first for batch endpoints; automatic model variant fallback when 95th/99th latency thresholds breach.

Suggested SLO matrix (attached: summit_slo_matrix.xlsx)
- P50 / P95 / P99 targets per endpoint class (interactive, async-batch) — see attachment for proposed breakouts and monitoring hooks.

Immediate next steps (owner in brackets)
- I’ll share the SLO matrix and a draft topology diagram (attached). [sergio]
- Confirm which exact endpoints need interactivity SLA vs batch SLA (list of path patterns). [Maya / Rahul]
- Schedule a 90-minute technical workshop with your infra + security + our runtime engineers (proposed: Aug 25 or 26). [all]
- Procurement intro: please share procurement contact and timeline (we can attach a draft estimate & MSA). [Maya]

Compliance note: You asked for SOC 2 artifact checklist — Neha will loop in with the security pack once we confirm residency requirements.

Attachments: summit_slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO grid), redwood_dedicated_topology.png (draft), redwood-dedicated-estimate.pdf (ballpark).

If I’ve missed anything or misstated a requirement, please flag. Otherwise I’ll book the workshop and circulate a calendar invite for Aug 25/26.

Thanks,

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

[Attachment: summit_slo_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_topology.png (image/png)]
From: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@summithealth.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@summithealth.ai>, Carla Mendes <carla.mendes@summithealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Summit Health — topology & SLOs: post-call summary + action items

Sergio — thanks for the very clear summary. This matches our notes. A few clarifications and items from our side: 

Confirmed items
- We absolutely need P99 <= 350 ms for the clinician interactive flows. The consumer-facing triage tool can tolerate higher P99 (~800 ms) but we'd prefer lower.
- Nightly batch windows are flexible but need throughput guarantees; we’ll provide a sample daily load profile prior to the workshop.

Questions / asks
1) Data residency: We must keep PHI in US regions only. Does the Dedicated plan guarantee this with an option for VPC peering and customer-managed KMS?
2) Can you share an expected cost band (monthly) for the proposed dedicated topology for our expected baseline (est. 300 reqs/min steady)? A rough range is fine for the workshop.

Workshop attendees (please include these on the invite):
- Rahul Singh, CTO (rahul.singh@summithealth.ai)
- Carla Mendes, Head of Infrastructure (carla.mendes@summithealth.ai)
- Jonah Reed, Procurement (jonah.reed@summithealth.ai) — procurement will handle contract timelines

We’re available Aug 25 (10:00–13:00 PT) or Aug 26 (09:00–12:00 PT). Prefer Aug 25 if that works for your team. I’ll also circulate our sample traces and a short anonymized dataset for perf tuning prior to the meeting.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

—Maya
Director of Product, Summit Health
maya.gupta@summithealth.ai
[Attachment: sample_traces_anon.zip (referenced)]
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Summit Health — topology & SLOs: post-call summary + action items

Looping in a quick internal plan so we can move after the workshop: 

Internal action items
- Prep: Sergio/Neha to finalize SLO matrix and topology notes before the workshop (send to Rahul/Carla by EOD Aug 24). [sergio, neha]
- Pricing: I’ll prepare a 3-tier estimate (pilot / production-dedicated / dedicated-with-fallback) and include expected monthly run-rate and consumption sensitivity. Attach: redwood-dedicated-estimate.pdf. [rachel]
- Compliance: Neha, please prepare SOC 2 artifact checklist and confirm KMS options for US-region-only keys. [neha]
- Contracts: I’ll have a draft PSA/MSA and redline guide available after workshop; procurement contact is Jonah Reed per Maya.
- Technical workshop: Confirmed provisional booking for Aug 25 10:00–11:30 PT with runtime + infra + security. Will finalize calendar invite once Sergio confirms internal engineer availability.

Notes: For the canary strategy we should propose automatic model-variant fallback (70B -> 13B) and per-route circuit breaker thresholds; ops should have an opt-in autoscaling policy with burst capacity and observability hooks (token-level cost + tail-latency alerts).

I’ll attach the estimate now and start a HubSpot task against DEAL-2026-1863.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
